cases.requirement: Conformance targets only the exact pinned Harness rc5 baseline; newer/default-branch behavior is not protocol authority.
The deployment explicitly requires toolsFinalResultObserver support before relying on M4-043.
For Adapter DSH, live tools/result is the authoritative final ToolRuntime outcome source.
A direct tool-body return is intermediate evidence and cannot be used as final result authority.
A tools/post-execute replacement precedes final authority and the replaced materialized result is what tools/result exposes.
Definition-owned final-content transformation occurs before tools/result authority when the public rc5 seam exercises it.
ToolRuntime notifies tools/result with the exact finalResult object that its finalization path returns.
Adapter resultDigest is computed from the exact authoritative tools/result result rather than the body return or an earlier candidate.
A final successful result maps to one correlated tool.completed success event.
A real body throw is materialized and observed through tools/result as final error authority.
A post-execute block/failure cannot leave an earlier successful body result authoritative.
A finalization/materialization failure becomes the authoritative materialized error rather than falling back to an earlier success.
Policy ALLOW, approval allowed-once, hard-guard abstention, or body entry cannot by themselves synthesize execution success.
Policy/guard/approval disposition metadata may classify an authoritative final result but does not replace the final result or its digest source.
One agent-backed native tools/result notification observed by one active Adapter subscription emits one live normalized tool.completed, absent normalization failure.
The later durable session tool/result fact does not produce a second live tool.completed for the same native completion.
Final-result correlation uses exact sessionRef from exec.agent.session.id, callRef from exec.callId, and toolName from exec.name.
M4-043 does not infer portable actionRef, Subject lineage, or replacement call identity from Harness execution ids.
An agent-less tools/result does not cause the Adapter to synthesize a session-scoped tool.completed event.
Harness freezes the live execution object before tools/result observers receive it.
tools/result is an emit-style observation seam and cannot replace the already-final ToolRuntime result.
A synchronous tools/result observer throw is contained and does not alter the returned final result.
An asynchronous tools/result observer rejection is contained and does not alter the returned final result.
Adapter normalization/reporting failure is observation failure and must not mutate ToolRuntime's authoritative result.
Disposing an Adapter observation subscription prevents future tools/result delivery through that subscription.
Replay reconciliation and durable recovery remain separate from the live tools/result authority path.
M4-043 does not standardize the result digest algorithm; it standardizes only the authoritative digest input source.
Observing a final result does not authorize raw-result persistence or weaken M4-045 audit-redaction requirements.
A successful ToolRuntime result does not prove every claimed external effect occurred or that every host effect traversed ToolRuntime.
A failed ToolRuntime result does not prove external side effects were rolled back or absent.
M4-043 does not establish provider/process isolation or complete system-wide tool-enforced coverage.
M4-043 does not implement M4-044 approval uniqueness, M4-045 redaction, later negative-boundary tests, or PR merge authority.
